Sewers / Trenchless

Trenchless Sewer Technology

Modern no-dig sewer repair using pipe bursting and lining.

A bursting head is pulled through the old pipe. It breaks the old pipe outward into the soil while a new, seamless pipe follows right behind it.

The repair happens underground, not across your yard.

Open trench

Digging
A trench along the whole line
Your yard
Lawn, driveway and plants torn up
Time on site
Often several days or more
Cleanup
Heavy restoration afterwards

Trenchless

Digging
One or two small access pits
Your yard
Mostly left as it is
Time on site
Often a day or two
Cleanup
Fill the pits and tidy up

How a job goes

  1. 1

    Camera inspection

    We run a camera through the line to see the damage, the pipe material and the length of the problem.

  2. 2

    Small access points

    We dig one or two small pits at the ends of the section, often near the cleanout or the property line.

  3. 3

    Burst or line

    We pull a new pipe through, or cure a new liner inside the old one, depending on the condition of the pipe.

  4. 4

    Test and reconnect

    We check the new pipe with the camera, test the flow, reconnect your fixtures and fill the pits.

Which method fits your pipe

The camera inspection decides it. Here is what each method is good at.

Pipe bursting

Replaces the old pipe with a brand new one, the same size or larger.

A good fit for

  • Collapsed or crushed pipe
  • Pipe that has shifted or sagged
  • Heavy root damage along the line
  • Old clay or cast iron beyond repair

Not ideal when

  • Other utilities running very close to the pipe

Pipe lining

Builds a new pipe inside the old one without removing it.

A good fit for

  • Cracks, leaks and open joints
  • Roots getting in at the joints
  • Pipe that is still in line and open
  • Lines under driveways or patios

Not ideal when

  • Collapsed or badly shifted pipe

Common questions

Do you have to dig up my yard?+

Only the small access pits. Everything between them stays in place.

Can it fix a collapsed pipe?+

Pipe bursting can, because it replaces the pipe. Lining usually can't, since the old pipe has to be open enough to line.

Will the repair last?+

Both methods use materials made to last for decades. A camera check after the job shows us the result before we close up.

Can your line be fixed without digging?

We'll put a camera in the pipe and tell you which method fits, and whether you need one at all.
